# the contributor audit: finite interval elimination and the signed menu matrix

PASS for the complete proofs in candidate 44be6cdd33cc2f74 and signed-thin-edge-descent-and-menu-dependent-affine-moment-matrix-optimal-midpoint.md. the contributor reran the finite-path verifier: all 48,630 exact rational checks passed.

## Finite interval path

Canonical replacement is an actual continuous Minkowski path between nested bodies with identical integer fibers, so every measured fiber stays fixed. The base reflection and continuous-coordinate shear are legitimate coordinate normalizations; conjugating the later path returns it to the original coordinates. Compatibility is exactly the two printed midpoint bounds. The archived exact cap-depth formula, rather than a selected-center estimate, controls all source changes.

Increasing the middle shift to the supporting contact makes all three branches nonincreasing. On that contact, the printed three middle-depth branches agree at their seams. Their normalized derivatives with respect to the smaller endpoint length have the three correct positive numerators. If the large endpoint is already deepest, increasing middle length to the tie keeps raw maximum fixed and increases total volume. Every positive tie lies on the first branch, at U=b-2a with a<=b/5. Following that tie as a decreases keeps both raw depths b/2 while total mass 2b-a increases. If a vanishes first, U>=b and reducing U to b decreases U/[2(U+b)]. The zero-length endpoint has zero measured depth and remains an actual fiber; the other two fibers keep Hausdorff dimension one throughout. No candidate point or boundary fiber is silently dropped.

## Signed thin-edge escape and finite-dimensional alternative

The finite-cap envelope lemma uses compact attainment, uniqueness, positive spanning of the gradients, and uniform differentiability to force optimizing displacements O(t). Only then is the balanced first-order average used; it does not presume a differentiable optimizer. In the thin-edge body all five direction cones can be represented by one positive circuit. High caps can independently choose the same strictly captured endpoint; low caps retain strict misses. Antisymmetric endpoint homotheties preserve the exact Minkowski average, central fiber, and complete integer projection. Both total mass and the actual covariance numerator are even. The divergence theorem supplies precisely d times endpoint volume. Thus the full response and actual maximum-depth descent are correctly obtained, including competing endpoint candidates.

For fixed menus, the affine rows include the exact covariance correction and normalized mass derivative. Their finite convex-hull separation is equivalent to simultaneous signed improvement. The compact menu sets give the stated equivalence between every menu selection having a cancelling multiplier and every signed direction having a source with nonpositive optimized response. This does not exchange the menu and multiplier quantifiers. No new lattice inequality follows merely from the matrix formulation.
